Opening

GROW · RE & World Views · Autumn 1 · Week 1

Beliefs and worldviews in our community

Learning goal

Identify different beliefs and worldviews in our community.

How do beliefs and festivals show what matters to people?

I can name different worldviews, explain a festival symbol, compare two festivals and explain a shared value.

40 minutes, with flexible pauses. Point, speak, draw, type or write. A fictional example is welcome. Nobody is asked to share a personal belief.

Editable Word packPrintable pupil resources PDF

This is learning about religion and worldviews, not worship. Nobody is asked to share a personal belief, family detail or loss.

Arrival

GROW · RE & World Views · Autumn 1 · Week 1

Arrival task

You can begin without previous learning. Word help: religion means an organised set of beliefs, practices and community.

Start with 1 and 2. Continue with 3 and 4 when ready.

1. What does religion mean?

Help

Use the reminder strip or talk it through with an adult.

An organised set of beliefs, practices and community

2. Which meaning fits religion?

Help

Choose: An organised set of beliefs, practices and community OR The way a person sees life and what matters.

An organised set of beliefs, practices and community

3. Name two different worldviews found in Britain.

Help

Use the model evidence anchor A, C or read one relevant card together.

Any two, for example Christianity and Humanism.

4. Does a non-religious person have beliefs and values?

Help

Give a reason when ready.

Yes. Everyone has a worldview, religious or not.

Word and evidence bank

A Hannah

Fictional profile: Hannah is 14 and Christian. She goes to church with her gran and prays before exams. She says her faith helps her stay calm.

Authored profile

Limit: This is one person's view. Others who share the worldview may describe it differently.

B Imran

Fictional profile: Imran is 15 and Muslim. He prays, fasts in Ramadan and helps at a mosque food bank.

Authored profile

Limit: This is one person's view. Others who share the worldview may describe it differently.

C Ellie

Fictional profile: Ellie is 14 and non-religious. She calls herself a Humanist. She thinks people should use reason and kindness to decide what is right.

Authored profile

Limit: This is one person's view. Others who share the worldview may describe it differently.

D Worldviews in Britain

The 2021 census for England and Wales found Christianity was the most common religion, and about 37% of people said they had no religion. Islam, Hinduism, Sikhism, Judaism and Buddhism were also recorded.

Authored summary of Office for National Statistics census 2021 headline results

Limit: A census counts what people tick. It cannot show how they live their beliefs.

Independent application

Choose one route and one response mode. Keep the same learning goal.

Supported task

  1. Place two profile cards on the community map.
  2. Label each with its worldview from the word bank.
  3. Point to one clue for each.

Read one evidence card together. Highlight a useful detail. Rehearse with: One worldview in our community is ___. A clue is ___. Complete the organiser one space at a time. One worldview in our community is ___. A clue is ___.

An adult may read or scribe your exact response. They should not choose the answer.

Standard task

  1. Place the three fictional profiles on the community map.
  2. Label each worldview.
  3. Add one clue from each profile.

One worldview in our community is ___. A clue is ___.

Check the required evidence and revise one detail.

Stretch task

  1. Complete the map with all three profiles and clues.
  2. Add one fact from the census card.
  3. Explain what a census cannot tell us about belief.

Choose the evidence independently. Use the frame only if it helps.

Explain why a non-religious person still has a worldview.

Teacher brief

Teacher notes and answers

Teacher card

Beliefs and worldviews in our community / GROW_RE_A1_W01

Outcome: Identify different beliefs and worldviews in our community.

Evidence to retain: F: community-worldviews map naming two worldviews.

Forty minute route

Arrival 4 min; starter 3; model 6; shared task 7; check 2; independent 12; review 3; exit 3. Pause time is flexible.

Preparation

Choose one independent route. Print the evidence and shared cards, required visual or data sheet, route worksheet and exit. The organiser is one separate A4 page. Keep answers with staff.

Mode! neutral language; no cold calling; use ‘some/ many/this person’; check vocabulary before independent task; allow pointing before speaking/writing.

Access and regulation

Short text; visual icons; 2-option choices; sentence stems; verbal/scribed response; typing option; no personal belief disclosure required.

Offer a predictable start, private response and agreed pause. No cold calling or forced personal disclosure. Rejoin at one clearly named next step. Keep teen-appropriate examples and the same learning goal across response modes.

This is learning about religion and worldviews, not worship. Nobody is asked to share a personal belief, family detail or loss.

Assessment

Use questioning and the exit response to decide the next step. Record the learner’s individual contribution and the access support used.

UAS: no approved unit code is supplied. Match the learner’s evidence to the centre-selected unit and exact criteria before submission. This pack makes no automatic award claim.

Model and answers

Read these pages before teaching. Hide the model during independent assessment.

Question: Name two different worldviews found in Britain.

Evidence: A Hannah: Fictional profile: Hannah is 14 and Christian. She goes to church with her gran and prays before exams. She says her faith helps her stay calm. C Ellie: Fictional profile: Ellie is 14 and non-religious. She calls herself a Humanist. She thinks people should use reason and kindness to decide what is right.

Think aloud: Any two, for example Christianity and Humanism.

Check: Does a non-religious person have beliefs and values? Yes. Everyone has a worldview, religious or not.

Arrival answers

1. An organised set of beliefs, practices and community

2. An organised set of beliefs, practices and community

3. Any two, for example Christianity and Humanism.

4. Yes. Everyone has a worldview, religious or not.

Shared activity reasoning

1. Prays before exams and goes to church — Christian. Card A: Hannah goes to church and prays.

2. Fasts in Ramadan — Muslim. Card B: Imran fasts in Ramadan.

3. Uses reason and kindness, follows no religion — Humanist. Card C: Ellie is non-religious and a Humanist.

Exit responses

Name two different worldviews found in Britain. Any two, for example Christianity and Humanism.

Does a non-religious person have beliefs and values? Yes. Everyone has a worldview, religious or not.

Teaching and evidence record

Supplied scheme of work teaching sequence: Arrival: 4 short retrieval/misconception questions about religion, belief, worldview and community. Starter: image sort — religious / non-religious / unsure. I Do: introduce the idea of a worldview using short lived examples. We Do: match people/profiles to beliefs or worldview clues. You Do: create a simple community-worldviews map using fictional profiles. Exit ticket: name two different worldviews found in Britain.

Look for

F: community-worldviews map naming two worldviews.

Accept accurate equivalents, including speech or exact scribing. Check the concept and use of evidence rather than length or handwriting. Record access support separately from content prompting.

BUILD: a concrete example with a reason or demonstrated action. GROW: explain or compare with a relevant detail. LAUNCH: connect evidence and reasoning; use a limitation when the outcome requires it. Keep RE responses non-GCSE.

Media

Original captioned teaching model made for this pack. It demonstrates the supplied reasoning; it is not historical footage, survivor testimony or a documentary. The full transcript and factual source credits are included.

Use manual steps for a calm pace. The silent MP4 has visible captions and a matching text transcript. External archive media is optional and should be previewed before class.
